questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Somnath temple:

1. Somnath temple is the holy place of Shree Somnath Mahadev which is the first Adi Jyotirling.

2. It was first raided and destroyed by Muhammed Ghori during the reign of Bhima I.

3. Modern Somnath Temple was inaugurated by Sardar Patel in 1951.

Which of the following is/are correct***?***
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Only one.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Indian Express: Somnath: A brief history of the temple, and why Nehru opposed the President inaugurating it. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__****Somnath temple:**

 
• **The Somnath temple or Deo Patan,** is a Hindu temple **located in Prabhas Patan, Veraval in Gujarat, India. **It is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for Hindus and is the first among the twelve jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva.
 
• **Somnath means "Lord of the Soma" or "moon".**
 
• It is the holy place of** Shree Somnath Mahadev which is the first Adi Jyotirling**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The temple was reconstructed several times in the past after repeated destruction by multiple Muslim invaders and rulers,** notably starting with an attack by Mahmud Ghazni in the 11th century.** ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The contemporary Somnath temple's **reconstruction was started under the orders of the first Deputy Prime Minister of India, Vallabhbhai Patel** after receiving approval for reconstruction from Mahatma Gandhi. The reconstruction was completed in May 1951, after his death.
 
• **On 11 May 1951, Rajendra Prasad, the first President of the Republic of India, invited by K M Munshi, performed the installation ceremon**y for the temple. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **The site is also called Prabhasa ("place of splendor").** The Somnath temple is not mentioned in ancient Sanskrit texts of Hinduism, but the "Prabhasa-Pattana" is mentioned as a tirtha (pilgrimage site).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17750efbae898ca2abf20a2d8e2a0acf4367d60d4d3ca1b99092acd766b30c12.png]

questions.question: Which of the following tribes are known for "Rai dance"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bediya**__.

__
 
• **'Rai dance' is performed by women of the Bediya tribe in Bundelkhand of Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Bediya tribe** is a **nomad tribe** and has been nominated to the Scheduled Tribes in the 2011 census.
 
• Bediya tribes reside mainly in **Bundelkhand province of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• The women of the Bediya tribe indulge in prostitution. Rai dance is an integral part of their lifestyle.
 
• The men of the Bediya tribe do prostitution as a business from their families' sisters and daughters.
 
• In Bundeli folk dances, the women of this tribe are also called 'Bedni'.
 
• **Binjhwar tribe** is found in the Raipur and Bilaspur region of the **Central Provinces.**

questions.question: The annual Indian Classical music festival Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav is held in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pune.**__

 
• The **Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav** is an annual** 'Indian Classical music festival'** held in **Pune, Maharashtra.**
 
• It was** started by Bhimsen Joshi** in 1953.
 
• It is organized by the disciples of Sawai Gandharva in collaboration with 'Arya Sangeet Prasar Mandal' and continues for **3 days.**
 
• This festival was earlier known as the '**Sawai Gandharva Music Festival'**.
 
• Artists from all regions of India including singers, dancers, and musicians participate in the event.
 
• **Rambhau Kundgolkar** is known as **"Sawai Gandharva".**

questions.question:
Which contemporary painter made a series of paintings on Mahatma Gandhi?

A. Amrita Shergill

B. Ram Kinkar

C. M.F. Hussain

D. Atul Dodiya
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct.

__
 
• **Atul Dodiya**__ made a series of paintings on **Mahatma Gandhi**. 
 
• He is considered one of the finest Indian artists of the generation.
 
• He is known for his Hyper-realist depictions of middle-class Indian life, Series of watercolor paintings depicting marginalized and poor sections of society, for example, a plumber, a scribe, or a painter, etc.
 
• In 1991, he reconstructed images from a forgotten biography of Mahatma Gandhi. He used watercolors to paint numerous historic events of Gandhi's life.
 
• He also installed "Broken Branches" made in 2002 inspired by the philosophy of Mahatma Gandhi in Venice Biennale 2019 (art exhibition).

questions.question: ‘Rongali Bihu’ one of the major festival of Assam is celebrated in the month of______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April.**__

 
• **Bohag Bihu **Or **Rongali Bihu** is one of the major festivals of** Assam.**
 
• Commonly known as **Rongali Bihu**, it is celebrated in **Assam** during the middle of the month of **April.**
 
• This festival celebrates the onset of the** Assamese New Year (around April 15) **and the **coming of Spring.**
 
• This marks the** first day of the Hindu solar calendar **and is also observed in Bengal, Manipur, Nepal, Orissa, Punjab, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu though called by different names like **Pongal in south India**, **Baisakhi in north India.** This festival celebrated for the whole month.
 
• The** new year** of the **Assamese calendar** usually falls on **April 15**. The new year starts with the month **Bohag. **This is the reason why **Rongali Bihu is also called Bohag Bihu.**
 
• The word** Rongali** is derived from **Rong **which means** Happiness and celebrations**. So this festival represents the happiness of society. 
 
• On the eve of **Rongali Bihu,** the** womenfolk clean the clothes and prepare special Bihu delicacies like Chira, Pitha, etc. **In the rural areas, the **menfolk remain busy in collecting necessary items such as Tara Pogha (ropes for the cattle)** prepared out of slices of Tara (an indigenous creeper) and vegetables such as raw turmeric, brinjal, gourd, etc for the next day's Garu Bihu.

questions.question: Which community of Manipur celebrates the Gaan Ngai festival every year after the harvest season?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is __**Zeliangrong.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gaan Ngai festival** is a major event in **Manipur**, celebrated by the **Zeliarong** community every year after the** harvest season.**
 
• On January 4, 2023, the community came together to **show their gratitude for a good harvest and pray for a prosperous year ahead.**
 
• The festival is celebrated for a **full 5 days**, usually in the** month of December or January.**
 
• The exact **date varies **from year to year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The festival also **marks the end of the year **when the farmers have stored their foodgrain in their granaries.
 
• It is a custom to **produce new fire by rubbing dry wood and split bamboo pieces** and distributing them to every household on the day of the festival to mark the beginning of the new year.
 
• The Zeliarong community in Manipur comprises **Rongmei, Liangmei, and Zeme tribes.**

questions.question: For how many days, is the Karaga Utsav depicting the religious heritage and rich culture of Karnataka celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karaga festival is celebrated in the state of Karnataka.**
 
• This Festival is one of the **oldest festivals in Karnataka** with a hi**story of over 300 years.**
 
• The festival is celebrated **annually in march or April (Chaitra Month according to the Hindu Calander).**
 
• The** festival runs for 11 days **and is a celebration of rituals and traditions that have their origin in the epic Mahabharata, particularly in the stripping of Draupadi.
